trace.goal: Surface hidden operational problems with multi-agent deployment.
expected_facts: The answer should focus on real operational friction, not futuristic speculation.
It should cover issues like supervision, drift, orchestration, or workflow brittleness.
It should frame these as solvable but under-discussed execution challenges.
rubric_must_haves: Keeps the focus on operating reality.
Includes at least one issue beyond prompt quality alone.
trace.gold_reference: A strong answer should explain that once many AI agents are live, the hard problems shift from demos to operations: monitoring, coordination, reliability, stale data, and human oversight. The point is that multi-agent systems create a new management surface area that most teams underestimate. Founders should treat these as production issues, not side notes.

trace.answer: We have 30+ AI agents deployed across our entire business now. Not just sales tools, not just support chatbots — real production agents managing critical workflows like sponsor operations, content review, and event planning. And after four months of this, I've identified five problems nobody talks about when they're hyping AI agent deployments. Problems everyone hits hard. Problem #1: The Data Ingestion Nightmare Nobody Warns You About This was my biggest surprise. Every single agent requires some form of data ingestion. Some demand massive datasets upfront before they'll even work properly. Others need constant updates throughout the day. What we learned: you cannot buy an agent without thinking through your data pipeline first. What kind of data does it require? How often do you need to update it? Who owns that process? Most vendors don't even want to talk about this. They'd rather sell you on their magical "intelligence" than admit their product needs clean, structured data to function. Our solution: treat data ingestions as a full-time job for someone who understands your systems. If you're a founder reading this, start budgeting for a dedicated "AI Operations Manager" role immediately. Someone whose sole responsibility is feeding these agents clean data. It's not glamorous, but it's essential. Problem #2: The Training Time That Vendors Downplay Terrible mistake most founders make: underestimating training time. Many agents promise "plug-and-play" experiences that never actually exist. The reality varies wildly depending on complexity and quality of vendor documentation. Our experience: plan for weeks of intense daily investment instead
trace.raw_model_output: We Have 30 AI Agents in Production. Here Are the Top 5 Issues No One Talks About When we started using AI agents six months ago, everything seemed simple enough. Just pick an agent, train it on our data, watch magic happen. Fast forward to today—after 10,000+ conversations across multiple platforms—and here’s what I’ve learned: this stuff is hard. Not because the technology doesn’t work (it does). But because nobody tells you about all the hidden problems until you’re already drowning in them. So let me save you some time and share the five things no one warns you about when you start your AI journey. #1: Your Team Won't Actually Adopt It. They'll Pretend To. And Then Ignore You This was my biggest surprise. Everyone talks about AI transformation like it’s easy—you just deploy an agent and suddenly everyone’s a convert. That’s completely wrong. After two years of trying every approach imaginable (including gamification campaigns), I've learned the truth: People don't want change. They pretend they're excited for weeks while secretly hoping it goes away. The reality? Most folks just tune out once initial questions get answered. Why? Because they genuinely believe they know more than they actually do, which leads to "I'm good" responses instead of honest questions. What actually works? Start small. Pick something so obvious that even skeptics have to admit you're right. For us, it was outbound—it literally cannot be ignored anymore. From there, build trust gradually. Don't force adoption. Let people find their own use cases

#5. Launch Your First AI Agent That Actually Works.  And That You Can Really Sell.
Not an AI feature. Not a chatbot. A real AI agent that handles actual workflows end-to-end.
I’ve deployed 20+ AI agents across SaaStr’s operations. Support agents. Content agents. Sales qualification agents. Together they’ve generated over $1M in revenue while reducing our headcount needs.
Most founders are still debating whether to add AI to their product. That’s table stakes now. The real question is: are you using AI agents to fundamentally transform your own operations?
Because here’s what I’m seeing: companies deploying working AI agents are operating with 30-50% fewer humans in key functions. Customer support. Sales development. Content creation. Implementation. Legal review.
Those aren’t future capabilities. They’re working today. At scale. And if you’re not deploying them, your competitors are.
Launch one high value agent in Q1. Get it working. Learn. Then launch two more by end of year.
The companies that figure out AI agents first will have massive cost advantages and speed advantages over everyone else. Don’t wait.
How we manage 20+ AI Agents without them stepping all over each other ...

#5.  Our AI Can Help You Figure Out What To Do About Churn and Other Issues
Share all your challenges and metrics, and our AI will help come up with a game plan for you.

At SaaStr AI 2026, we answer that. With receipts.

May 12-14. SF Bay.
